A wake up message to myself.

I personally believe that some of us need to wake up and face the fact that we are our own greatest enemy. It's a hard pill to swallow, but it's the truth.

I'm currently 21 and I can say that I've made a lot of mistakes not because I needed to learn, but because I was just genuinely afraid.

## The answer has always been within you
What is that fear? can't you see that this "emotion" is a trap?[^1]



- Pay the price!
- Read that book, study that course!
- Express your feelings to that opposite gender! 
- Actually accept your destiny and do what is necessary to get there!!

## Will you be broken in the process? Possibly! Will you cry? Possibly.

But  keep` on pushing, there where so many times I thought I was wasting my strength learning design even tho I had a B.Sc in Software engineering. But I knew where I was going, I knew where I wanted to see myself. I told myself that I will build and design, I will be the one to build and design. Even tho you don't see the results yet, doesn't mean you have to stop.

## What nobody tells you

The race is not to the swift! No matter how fast you start, it doesn't determine the outcome, No matter how slow you start, it doesn't determine the outcome. It's about consistency! It's about never giving up! It's about finishing the race! [^3]

## Why I keep doing it

When I'm working on Forge, I can have an idea over breakfast and hold it in my hand, running on my phone, by the evening. I don't think I'll ever get tired of that.

Design taught me to care about the person on the other side of the screen. Engineering taught me to respect what it takes to put something there. I'd like to keep getting better at both, and I'll keep writing about it here as I go.

## Writing an entry

Create a Markdown file in `src/content/journal/`. The file name becomes the URL — `my-first-note.md` is served at `/journal/my-first-note`.

Every entry starts with frontmatter:

```yaml
title: My first note
date: 2026-09-20
excerpt: One sentence shown in lists and link previews.
tags: [design, engineering]   # optional
draft: false                  # optional, defaults to false
```

What an agency does day to day, and how well it runs, is hard to see before you're inside.

Structured breakdowns of specific agencies — workflow, structure, and how they actually operate. Being genuinely useful about a small thing beats being vague about everything.

A faith app for youth communities, and the portal churches run it with: scripture, sermons that keep playing, and a prayer wall the whole room sees.

  Forge is early. As you learn more, add:

  - <Stats> with real usage numbers once you have them

<Section id="problem" label="The problem" title="Faith apps felt like homework, and churches couldn't reach anyone in the moment">

Content arrived as long pages of text. When a church asked for prayer, there was no way for young people to see it, let alone answer while it still mattered.

<Insights>
<Insight title="Static text walls">
Long pages of scripture and notes, with nothing built for how young people actually read on a phone.
</Insight>
<Insight title="No live connection">
A prayer request reached nobody until the next service.
</Insight>
<Insight title="Drifting handoffs">
The designs and the shipped app slowly stopped matching each other.
</Insight>
<Insight title="Scattered admin">
Churches juggled separate tools to post devotionals and moderate their community.
</Insight>
</Insights>

</Section>

<Section id="solution" label="Solution" title="One ecosystem instead of scattered tools">

A Flutter app for members, a React portal for churches, and one API behind both: live prayer over Socket.IO, sermons that keep playing in the background, and design tokens that come straight from Figma.

<Stats>
<Stat value={3} label="connected tiers: mobile app, admin portal, and API" />
<Stat value={9} label="technologies across the stack" />
</Stats>

</Section>

<Section id="gallery" label="Gallery" title="Every screen, side by side">

<ScreenGrid items={props.gallery} slots={["Church portal"]} />

</Section>

<Section id="architecture" label="How it's built" title="Three tiers, each with one clear job">

<Diagram
  caption="How the app, portal, API and database connect"
  placeholder="System design image"
  parts={["App", "Portal", "Load balancer", "API", "MongoDB", "Socket.IO"]}
/>

The app and the portal both talk to one Express API. It decides who may do what, keeps everything in MongoDB, pushes new prayers over Socket.IO, and serves sermon media through a Multer pipeline on Render. The app itself is Flutter with Riverpod, Material 3 and a background audio player; the portal is React 19 with Vite and Tailwind.

</Section>

<Section id="decisions" label="Design decisions" title="Four choices that shaped how Forge feels">

<Choice title="Design tokens flow straight from Figma into Flutter">

A Python script (`extract_tokens.py`) parses raw Figma JSON into Flutter `AppSpacing`, `AppColors` and typography constants, so spacing, colour and type come from the same place as the designs.

<Takeaway title="Why it matters">
Design changes reach the app through the pipeline instead of being re-typed by hand.
</Takeaway>

</Choice>

<Choice title="Prayer requests arrive the moment they're shared">

Socket.IO channels carry live prayer counters and group request chats, so young people can respond while it still matters, not at the next service.

</Choice>

<Choice title="Sermons keep playing when the app is in the background">

Background audio (`just_audio` and `audio_service`) and video playback (`chewie`) make a sermon something you can take with you on the walk home.

</Choice>

<Choice title="What you can do follows your role">

Refresh token rotation and role-based permissions for members, leaders and admins, so a church can hand out the portal without handing over everything.

</Choice>

</Section>

<Section id="reflection" label="Reflection" title="Still early, and learning from our first users">

Forge is at an early stage, with its first users just coming on board. The next chapter of this case study is what they teach us.

</Section>

</Section>

The extension parses a page in real time and extracts its tokens — colours, shadows, typography, and spacing — into clean JSON or CSS variables.

<Insights>

Extracts colours, shadows, fonts, and layout tokens directly from the page's DOM.
</Insight>
<Insight label="02" title="Ready to paste">
Copy tokens straight into CSS variables or Tailwind token formats.
</Insight>
